findings.note: Source (para B-4): 'beyond which all fires must be coordinated with affected commanders prior to engagement and, short of the line, all fires must be coordinated with the establishing commander'. The slide's first sentence drops 'beyond it', so it reads as a rule for all fires everywhere; the requirement loses its scope (planner rule 3) and short of the line it now adds a second coordination duty the source does not give.
findings.fix: Now: 'Fire support coordination line (FSCL) Beyond it, all fires must be coordinated with affected commanders first. Short of it, all fires must be coordinated with the commander who set it.'

findings.note: Source (para B-2): 'Such fires must still comply with ROE and law-of-war targeting constraints'. The talking point keeps the ROE half of the 'must' but drops the law-of-war half.
findings.fix: Now: 'A coordinated fire line is not permission to fire at anything: fires must still follow the rules of engagement and the law of war.'

findings.note: Source (para B-36): an RFA is a location 'into which fires that exceed those restrictions will not be delivered without coordination'. 'Fires past its limits' can be read as fires beyond the area's edges, not fires into it that break its restrictions. Directive word kept correctly.
findings.fix: Now: 'Restrictive fire area: fires into it that break its limits will not be delivered without coordinating with the HQ that set it.'

findings.note: Source (para 4-67): 'The computation of firing data must be accurate.' The slide adds 'computed with care' to the 'must'. It's harmless, but the source doesn't say it.
findings.fix: Now: 'Accurate computational procedures Firing data must be computed accurately'

findings.note: Source (para 4-67): 'projectile square weight, fuze type, and propellant temperature'. 'Propellant heat' is imprecise because the correction is for temperature, which can be cold as well as hot.
findings.fix: Now: 'Accurate weapon and ammunition information Round speed leaving the tube, round weight, fuze type, propellant temperature'

findings.note: The cited chapter intro (ch-3.t1) lists the four FS functions, FS processes and procedures, planning and coordination, rehearsals, execution and assessment. It does not mention 'targeting', even though chapter 3 does contain a targeting section (paras 3-30 to 3-34).
findings.fix: Now: 'This chapter covers fire support planning, coordination, rehearsals, and how fires are run and checked.'

findings.note: Source (para C-14): 'If one howitzer in the battery or platoon loses digital communications, the FDC will issue voice commands to that howitzer or the howitzer can fire data from an adjacent section.' The slide keeps the 'will' but drops the 'or' alternative, so an option becomes a single required action. A Soldier on the gun line would not know that firing data from the next section is allowed.
findings.fix: Now: 'If one howitzer loses its digital link, the fire direction center will send it voice commands, or it can fire data from the next section.'

findings.note: Source (para C-67): 'voice fire commands must be transmitted to one or more of the howitzers. If the failure is at the AFATDS, voice commands must be transmitted to each of the howitzers.' The slide's 'to the howitzers' reads as all howitzers in every case. It drops 'one or more' and the each-howitzer case when the failure is at the AFATDS.
findings.fix: Now: 'When the digital link fails, voice fire commands must be sent to the howitzers it affects.'

findings.note: Source (para 6-44.li4): 'Plan targets, observer positions (primary and alternate), triggers, and fires in support of all EAs for all phases of the defensive operation.' The slide drops '(primary and alternate)', 'fires' and 'for all phases'. Alternate observer positions matter to observers.
findings.fix: Now: 'For every engagement area and phase, plan targets, primary and alternate observer posts, triggers and fires.'

findings.note: Source (para 6-94): 'FA units move well forward prior to an attack, sometimes beyond the FLOT, displacing by echelon to provide continuous fires.' The slide drops 'prior to an attack', so the timing is lost.
findings.fix: Now: 'Before an attack, field artillery moves well forward. It moves a part at a time so fires never stop.'

findings.note: Glossary: danger close is a mandatory call 'alerting of an elevated risk to the closest friendly troops from the intended point of a weapon's impact requiring specific procedures for risk mitigation.' The slide drops that the call requires specific procedures to lower the risk, which is the action it triggers (safety term). 'A round' also narrows 'a weapon' (the source covers air-to-surface too).
findings.fix: Now: 'A mandatory call. It warns that the closest friendly troops are at higher risk from where a weapon is meant to hit. Specific procedures then lower the risk.'

findings.note: Rests on garbled table 3-1 ('Decide Mission Analysis ... Begin identifying high-payoff targets based on initial high-value target...'); alignment is plausible but not certain. 'High-payoff targets' is jargon not explained. Decide also covers developing the high-payoff target list, target selection standards and attack guidance matrix, so 'start identifying' is a narrow summary. Accepted: the Decide/Detect/Deliver step texts rest on table 3-1, which is garbled in the conversion; the adjudicator checked the cell alignment against the table text (Decide row: 'Begin identifying high-payoff targets...') and it matches. Term 'high-payoff targets' left as written; a plainer gloss would need text the source doesn't give here.
findings.fix: 'Decide: Pick the targets that matter most (high-payoff targets) and plan how to attack them.' Cite para-3-31 and table-3-1; or keep wording but add a one-line definition of high-payoff target from the doc tree.
